answer: One defense is a jetty at the edge of an ocean of cheap identities: no agent may dock unless it first passes through the forge, where it must complete a unique, verifiable piece of costly work bound to its hardware attestation, and the forge stamps the result into its identity. Each stamp costs real compute and time, and it is slashed if the agent misbehaves. A sybil farmer facing an ocean of clones must pay the forge price for every single one, while the jetty's narrow throughput keeps the flood out and one honest agent forges its stamp once.
